mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_LeastPrivilege removes the (role, op) ↔ outcome=Success linkage; the injection forces a successful operation whose (role, kind) cell is NOT in PermMatrix.Allowed — exactly what LeastPrivilege forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Success and ((op.caller.role -> op.kind) not in PermMatrix.Allowed) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the append-only fact removes the uniqueness constraint on (app, event_type); the injection forces two distinct events with identical (app, event_type) — a direct counterexample to append-only.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.app = e2.app and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_OnePendingPerCustomer lets a customer hold two Pending-Review applications simultaneously; the injection demands exactly that scenario.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoPendingPerCustomer { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the at-most-one-decision-per-app fact allows two Decision rows pointing at the same LoanApplication; the injection forces two such Decisions to exist, violating FR-011/FR-012.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoDecisionsSameApp { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.application = d2.application }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_OwnershipBasedAccess lets a customer's GetApplicationById succeed without a properly-owned target; the injection produces a customer Success on GetApplicationById with NO target, which the predicate insists must have an owned target — and F_NoInformationLeakage (which requires `some op.target`) does not constrain this case.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CustomerSuccessNoTarget { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = GetApplicationById and op.outcome = Success and no op.target }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AttributionCorrect removes the rule that a SubmittedEvent's actor must equal the application's customer; the injection forces a SubmittedEvent whose recorded actor differs from the application's customer.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SubmittedAttributionMismatch { some e: ApplicationEvent | e.eventType = SubmittedEvent and e.actor != e.app.customer }
